WHILE Shri Rama was still King of Ayodhya, the great Sage 
Valmiki composed this beautiful classic. 
The holy rishi composed twenty-four thousand verses and 
divided them into five hundred chapters and six books. In 
addition, he composed the epilogue. The work being completed,

sage, who had expounded the meaning of the scriptures in bis 
verses, taught the classic to them. 
The great Valmiki taught them the classic describing the 
deeds of Rama and Sita and all that relates to the inciden!B 
lesding to the slaying of Ravana named "The Slaying of the 
Grandson of Poulastya ".1 
Tbis historical classic is pleasant to 
sing and adopted to the three measures of time,' it is contained 
within the seven notes and can be sung to the vina. It expresses 
the various moods of love, courage, disgust, anget, terror,

The two princes were skilled musicians, proficient in rhythm

On a particular occasion, the two princes, great-souled,

Showetiag ptaises on the brothers, they cried, "How melodiously 
you sing I How exquisite is the divine poetn, the story of

Being pleased with the sweet singers, one sage presented them

thread, some vessels for collecting alms, others gave loin cloths, 
kusba grass, garments of yellow cloth, scarves and thread for

They said : " This metre will be the foundation of the verse

In the assembly, surrounded by his ministers and brothers,

Then Shri Rama commanded the two musicians to sing and

brief.summary_1line: Valmiki teaches the Ramayana to Rama’s sons, Lava and Kusha, who sing it before sages and eventually before Rama in his royal court.

image_candidates.scene_text: Lava and Kusha sit in Valmiki’s forest hermitage playing the vina while reciting the Ramayana before gathered sages.
In Rama’s grand court, the twin princes sing with their vinas as Rama listens from a golden throne surrounded by ministers and brothers.
Moved sages with tears of joy shower the young singers with fruits, robes of bark, rosaries, and blessings.
